card.name: scriptlook
card.summary: 上传 PDF/FDX/TXT，用自带 OpenAI/Claude 密钥做剧本分析，生成场景、角色、地点、道具、服装、故事板与海报等视觉内容；无账号、无数据库，密钥与项目存浏览器 localStorage。
card.positioning: 开源 BYOK 工具，把剧本或 treatment 转成可编辑的视觉方案 deck
card.scope: 面向学生、首次拍片者、短片与小团队的早期提案；明确不做预算、通告单与制片管理。

features.text: 剧本导入与浏览器内 PDF 文本提取（扫描件需先 OCR）
AI 生成场景、角色、地点、道具、服装与制作提示
可选 fal.ai 生成角色、地点、道具、故事板与海报图
浏览器内编辑、打印、存 PDF 与分享

license.note: 许可证完整正文与 SPDX 官方文本规范化精确匹配；未忽略附加条款。

conditions: 需接受 deck 形式而非标准拆解表
scenario_matches.reason: 可从剧本生成场景与元素拆解，但输出为视觉 deck，非分场拆解表
scenario_matches.scenario_description: 独立制片的一副导演拿到定稿剧本后，逐场标记演员、道具、服装与场地，生成分场拆解表，作为排期与预算的起点。

scenario_matches.reason: 含道具、服装等类别内容，但无部门级跨场元素报告与确认流程
scenario_matches.scenario_description: 道具或服装部门负责人查看本部门类别的跨场元素报告，逐条确认、补充备注，为采购与准备工作提供依据。

scenario_matches.reason: 未见剧本修订对比与保留标记功能
scenario_matches.scenario_description: 制片协调员导入修订版剧本，查看新增、拆分与被删场次，在保留原有标记的前提下核对拆解结果并重新分发。

sources.text:
Scriptlook

Turn a screenplay into a visual language.
Start with a screenplay or treatment, then develop its tone, storyboards, characters, locations, production design, posters, and visual identity.

Explore the live demo gallery →
Or use this repository to run the complete app with your own screenplay and API keys.

![The Scriptlook live demo gallery showing screenplay examples across several genres](docs/images/scriptlook-demo-gallery.webp) Scriptlook is an open-source, bring-your-own-key tool for filmmakers who want to turn a written project into an editable visual deck. For text and images, you'll need two keys: OpenAI or Claude for analysis and writing, and fal.ai for image generation. Upload a PDF, FDX, or TXT file, choose the sections you want, and Scriptlook builds a first-pass deck with creative direction, scenes, casting, locations, props, storyboards, posters, and early production thinking. Scriptlook works best for students, first-time filmmakers, short films, and small teams building an early pitch. It doesn't handle budgets, call sheets, or production management, and it isn't a substitute for creative judgment. ## What Scriptlook finds in a screenplay ### Film identity and tone The deck starts with the film's identity: logline, synopsis, themes, atmosphere, tonal descriptors, visual references, music and sound, color palette, title treatment, and poster directions. Together, these sections make the screenplay's tone easier to see and discuss. ![Hereditary example deck showing film identity, scope, atmosphere, tonal descriptors, and reference points](docs/images/hereditary-deck-01.webp) ![Hereditary example deck showing music and sound, color palette, similar moods, poster concepts, and cast](docs/images/hereditary-deck-02.webp) ![Hereditary example deck showing locations, production design, props, and scenes](docs/images/hereditary-deck-03.webp) [Explore the complete Hereditary example deck →](https://www.scriptlook.com/app/demo/hereditary) ### Characters and casting Scriptlook identifies each character, their role in the story, and their relationships, then develops casting and wardrobe references. The point is to make each character visually clear early enough to shape the rest of the deck.

*Casting references from [Emma](https://www.scriptlook.com/app/demo/emma#cast).* ### Locations and production design Locations, props, wardrobe, set requirements, continuity details, and practical risks all come from the same screenplay breakdown. This keeps the visual ideas tied to what the film will actually need.

*Production-design references from [The Lighthouse](https://www.scriptlook.com/app/demo/the-lighthouse#props).* ### Scenes and storyboards The scene map connects page ranges, characters, locations, props, emotional beats, production flags, and visual briefs. Optional storyboard frames add camera, lighting, composition, and mood references to each scene.

*Storyboard frames from [300](https://www.scriptlook.com/app/demo/300#scenes).* ### Posters and presentation Poster concepts reduce the film to one clear image and idea. The deck stays editable in the browser, so you can review, print, save it as a PDF, or share it as a working creative package.

*Poster directions from [Moonlight](https://www.scriptlook.com/app/demo/moonlight#poster-concepts), [Emma](https://www.scriptlook.com/app/demo/emma#poster-concepts), and [Aftersun](https://www.scriptlook.com/app/demo/aftersun#poster-concepts).* ## How it works 1. **Bring the screenplay.** Upload a text-based PDF, FDX, or TXT file. PDF text is extracted in the browser; scanned PDFs need OCR first. 2. **Build the breakdown.** Scriptlook uses your OpenAI or Claude key to turn the screenplay into structured scenes, characters, locations, props, themes, wardrobe, and production signals. 3. **Choose what to make.** Generate the sections you need using Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Gemini for writing. 4. **Generate the visuals.** Add a fal.ai key if you want to generate portraits, locations, props, storyboards, and poster concepts from the project's visual briefs. 5. **Shape the result.** Edit, regenerate, review, print, or share the deck from the browser. ## Run the full app locally You need Node.js 20.9 or newer and an API key from OpenAI or Claude for screenplay extraction. ```bash git clone https://github.com/madebysan/scriptlook.git cd scriptlook npm install npm run dev ``` Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000), go to **Settings**, and add the provider keys you want to use. - **OpenAI or Claude** — screenplay extraction and deck writing - **DeepSeek or Gemini** — optional alternatives for deck writing after extraction - **fal.ai** — optional storyboards, portraits, props, locations, and posters - **TMDB** — optional poster thumbnails for film and soundtrack references This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB. Scriptlook has no accounts, database, or analytics. It stores your provider keys and active project in your browser's `localStorage`. The original PDF is parsed in the browser. When you request generation, Scriptlook sends the extracted text and relevant project content only to the providers you chose. Check each provider's pricing and data policy before sending material you don't own or aren't allowed to process. For a production-style local run: ```bash npm run build npm start ``` ## Development Run the full local check before opening a pull request: ```bash npm test npm run typecheck npm run lint npm run build ``` ## License Scriptlook is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
